title: Prove the sharp two-axis native cutoff: widths 6–9
body:
For the two-axis affine/quadratic Gaussian monomial group, the exact stabilized tensor cutoff is **F=6**. Fixed register identities are decided by widths **6,7,8,9**, improving PR #5369's sufficient two-axis window of 8–11. This is sharp: an explicit fixed phase-projector × affine-sign residual vanishes at every width 1–8 but has a diagonal entry equal to one at width 9.

The proof identifies the exact phase-residue thresholds `(8,9,6,7)` and characterizes every complete test set: it must reach the appropriate threshold in each residue. The necessity argument uses `AGL(2,2)=S4` and its odd pointwise stabilizers; it closes the representation-kernel gap that a character-realization table alone would leave. The upper bounds have an analytic proof, with exact enumeration as corroboration. See `research/two-axis-native-cutoff/PROOF.md` and `RESULT.json`.

Validation passes: registered Python 3.12 replay, optimized replay, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official 14-file export and optimized Git-free replay with `PATH=/nonexistent`. Separate implementations check all 128 character minima against 625 count normal forms, 24 affine maps, 128 phase polynomials, all 15 stabilizers, 1,364 below-threshold ordered tuples, 2,856 phase sums, all four sharp witnesses and semantic controls.

This answers the **two-axis** portion of #5369's open least-cutoff question. It complements [Mihir Srivastava's active one-axis/general-proof audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5354#discussioncomment-19174027), which excludes least cutoffs for n>=2. No predecessor files, general-axis theorem, selected nine-axis supplier or κ are changed. Fixed external coefficients and complete dirty input/output endpoints remain essential; physical costs, full supplier admission, n>=3 and nonmonomial Clifford cutoffs remain outside this result. No human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

Credit Ali Romman's native cutoff theorem and open question, Jose Manuel's phase/native conventions, ywz65's affine-basis argument, Chris R's tensor-separation lineage and retained source contributors. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate automated proof/checker/review subagents, is disclosed. Fourier inversion and symmetric-group sign representations are classical; no global literature-priority claim.

[Canonical scoped result](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5354#discussioncomment-19174077). Base `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`; predecessor head `18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef`. Submission overlap covers 379 open PR bodies, 4,797 Discussion records and every base local note; no matching two-axis result found within that coverage.
